turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below that
MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K) using AT MOST 4 of the elements below
(set every other element to 0). Design variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])
  - Y (fraction in [0, 0.4])
  - Ca (fraction in [0, 0.272727])
  - La (fraction in [0, 0.78])
  - Bi (fraction in [0, 0.521978])
  - Fe (fraction in [0, 0.502513])
  - Nb (fraction in [0, 0.98])
  - C (fraction in [0, 0.972])
  - Pr (fraction in [0, 0.265043])
  - As (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - B (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Pb (fraction in [0, 0.5])
  - Ce (fraction in [0, 0.28])
  - Mo (fraction in [0, 1])
  - V (fraction in [0, 0.9918])
  - Zn (fraction in [0, 1])
  - Ni (fraction in [0, 0.6])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: O=0.348837, Cu=0.227273, Ba=0.166667, Sr=0.142857".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**Step 1 — Identify what drives high Tc in this dataset.**
Sorting the 300 samples by target, everything above ~100 K is a layered cuprate of the form (A)(Ba/Sr)₂(Ca)ₙ₋₁CuₙO_x:

| composition | Tc (K) |
|---|---|
| H2S1 | 185 (needs H, S — not available) |
| Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 | 132 (needs Hg) |
| **Ba2Ca2Cu3O** | **126** |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O | 120 (needs Tl) |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Sr2Ca2Cu3Li0.2O | 117 (needs Tl) |
| Tl1Ba1Ca1Cu2O5.5 | 114 (needs Tl) |
| Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 | 110 |
| Bi1.4Pb0.5Sb0.1Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 109 |
| Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 105.7 |

**Step 2 — Restrict to the allowed element menu (O, Cu, Ba, Sr, Y, Ca, La, Bi, …).**
Hg, Tl, Hg, S, H are all unavailable, so the Hg-1223 / Tl-1223 champions can't be reproduced. The **highest-Tc record in the data that is built *entirely* from allowed elements is `Ba2Ca2Cu3O` at 126 K** — a Ba–Ca–Cu–O "infinite-layer/1223-type" cuprate using exactly 4 elements (Ba, Ca, Cu, O). Bi-2223 type mixtures (Bi–Sr–Ca–Cu–O) would need 5 elements and top out near 105–110 K anyway; Y-123 (Y–Ba–Cu–O, 4 elements) tops out near 90–94 K.

**Step 3 — Check feasibility of the fractions.**
Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃O₁ → total 8 formula units:
- Ba = 2/8 = 0.25 (≤ 0.3333 ✓)
- Ca = 2/8 = 0.25 (≤ 0.2727 ✓)
- Cu = 3/8 = 0.375 (≤ 0.4545 ✓)
- O = 1/8 = 0.125 (≤ 0.6977 ✓)

Sum = 1.0, four elements, all other design variables 0. This sits exactly on the best allowed-element point in the training set (Ba–Ca–Cu–O family, Cu-rich, high Ca and Ba), so it is the composition most strongly supported by the data as a Tc maximizer — the trend (Cu-rich, Ca-containing, Ba-containing cuprate, no rare-earth dilution, no magnetic/pnictide substituents) is consistently the top of the ranking.

## Proposal

Final: O=0.125, Cu=0.375, Ba=0.25, Ca=0.25
